name: WHOT BRITISH
description: British variant of Whot, a Crazy Eights-style shedding game for two to six players. Use a Whot pack with five symbol suits and wild Whot cards; match suit or number on the play pile or draw from the stock. First to empty hand wins the round; penalty scoring over multiple rounds eliminates players who reach 100 points.

content.text: British variant of Whot, a Crazy Eights-style shedding game for two to six players. Use a Whot pack with five symbol suits and wild Whot cards; match suit or number on the play pile or draw from the stock. First to empty hand wins the round; penalty scoring over multiple rounds eliminates players who reach 100 points.

Whot was invented and trademarked by William Henry Storey of Southend-on-Sea, England, in 1935; first marketed by Storey & Co of Croydon, later acquired by Waddingtons and popular in Britain in the 1950s–1960s. The British version described here uses a 54- or 53-card pack; the game also became the national card game of Nigeria with variant rules.

A special Whot pack of 54 or 53 cards: five symbol suits (circle, triangle, cross, square, star) with uneven card counts per suit, plus four or five wild Whot cards (numbered 20). British packs from around 1990 often have four Whots (53 cards); earlier and Nigerian packs have five (54 cards).
Dealer deals six cards to each player one at a time; remainder forms the draw pile. First dealer is chosen by cutting the pack (lowest card deals, Whot counting 20).

items.text: Short game: One deal only; first player to get rid of all cards wins. No penalty scoring or elimination.
